## Summary

### Task
Fix the failing tests in the `taskflow/` package (an in-memory job-orchestration engine) by correcting logic bugs under `taskflow/`, without modifying `tests/`. The task is done when `python3 -m unittest` passes fully.

### Work done
The initial run had 18 failures out of 25 tests. I read the modules involved (`queue`, `retry`, `statemachine`, `scheduler`, `resources`, `config`, `dag`, `events`, `history`, `runner`) and compared each docstring with what the code actually did. I fixed seven root-cause bugs, using `sed` for each:

1. **`taskflow/queue.py`**, `_Entry.sort_key`: it returned `(self.seq, -self.priority)`, so ordering was FIFO only. It now returns `(-self.priority, self.seq)`, giving higher priority first with FIFO tie-breaks.
2. **`taskflow/retry.py`**, `RetryPolicy.should_retry`: `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1` was off by one. It is now `attempts_made < max_attempts`, so with `max_attempts=3`, retries are allowed after attempts 1 and 2 only.
3. **`taskflow/statemachine.py`**, `batch_order_ok`: `current >= prev` was inverted. It is now `current <= prev`, which enforces non-increasing priority within an admission batch. This bug was hidden behind the queue-ordering bug.
4. **`taskflow/resources.py`**, `ResourcePool.release`: `self.used -= 1` is now `self.used -= cost`. Resources were leaking, which stalled resource-limited pipelines.
5. **`taskflow/config.py`**, `deep_merge`: the recursive call had its arguments swapped, `deep_merge(value, result[key])`. It is now `deep_merge(result[key], value)`, so overrides win at the leaves.
6. **`taskflow/scheduler.py`**, `_cascade_skip`: it iterated `dag.dependents(...)`, which returns direct children only. It now uses `dag.transitive_dependents(...)`, so the whole downstream chain is skipped.
7. **`taskflow/events.py`**, `_prefix_matches`: it checked `prefix.startswith(topic + ".")`, which is backwards. It is now `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`. This fixed the `job.term` prefix subscription that feeds `History`'s failed, skipped and outcome-count queries.

### Current state
The last run of `python3 -m unittest` reported `Ran 25 tests ... OK`. No test files were modified.

### Next steps
No further fixes are required. If desired, I can re-run the suite once more as a final confirmation. I did not audit the modules that no test exercises (e.g. `planner`, `stats`, `metrics`, `filters`) for latent bugs, since they were outside the scope of the failing tests.
